target.title: fix: address update-card review findings (channel normalization, hidden-nav affordance, prerelease pinning, policy-aware bridge)
target.body:
Follow-up to #104171 (sidebar update card / app-first macOS update / Sparkle beta track), addressing all six post-merge P2 review findings on that PR.

## What Problem This Solves

The merged feature had six reviewer-confirmed gaps: a raw (untrimmed) `update.channel` read could bypass the extended-stable repair gate; users with a collapsed sidebar or closed mobile drawer lost their only update affordance; the exact-prerelease version rule applied only to `CLIInstaller.status()` while the launch resolver and validated-CLI cache still accepted a same-triple stable binary under a prerelease app; channel-policy (stable/beta/dev) managed installs advertised the Sparkle-first bridge although post-relaunch repair never runs for them; a click-time bridge decline ate the click without falling back to the gateway update; and a failed restart verification after a successful install fell through to a duplicate install prompt.

## Why This Change Was Made

- `OpenClawConfigFile.gatewayUpdateChannel()` now trims + lowercases at the owner; call sites compare plainly.
- app-host renders a floating `<openclaw-sidebar-update-card>` above the content when the navigation surface is hidden (collapsed desktop nav or closed mobile drawer) and nulls the sidebar wiring in that state so exactly one instance is active; shared localStorage dismissal covers both.
- New `Semver.satisfiesExpectedGatewayVersion(installed:expected:)` centralizes the prerelease-exact rule (any non-numeric dash suffix or alpha/beta lane, build metadata stripped) and is used by `CLIInstaller.classifyVersion`, `GatewayEnvironment.check()` (now compares raw normalized version strings), and `CommandResolver.validatedOpenClawExecutable`.
- `managedRepairGatesOpen` gains an `installPolicy` gate: exact pins keep the app as the gateway-version owner (Sparkle-first + auto-repair); channel policies close the bridge so the card drives `update.run`, which owns channel-floating installs.
- On click-time bridge decline the app now dispatches `openclaw:native-update-declined` into the webview after withdrawing the handler; the card listens and invokes the gateway update in the same click.
- After a successful install with unverified restart, the prompter returns early — the persisted pending-restart marker owns recovery instead of a stale-status duplicate prompt.

## User Impact

Extended-stable pins survive config formatting variants; updates stay reachable with hidden navigation; prerelease apps can no longer launch a same-train stable gateway from the validated cache; beta/dev-policy installs get working gateway updates from the card; no more dead first click after eligibility changes; no duplicate install dialog after a transient restart failure.

## Evidence

- `swift build` + full `swift test`: 1,008 tests / 130 suites pass; swiftlint + swiftformat clean.
- New/extended tests: `SemverTests` (prerelease predicate incl. rc/numeric-suffix/build-metadata), `CLIInstallerTests`, `CommandResolverTests` (validated-cache prerelease case), `UpdateOrchestrationTests` (padded/uppercase channel, policy gate cases, marker round-trip).
- jsdom: `app-host.test.ts` (floating card only when nav hidden, not during onboarding), `sidebar-update-card.test.ts` (declined-event fallback, no double-fire, listener cleanup) — 30 tests across 3 files pass.
- Fresh codex autoreview on the branch diff: clean, no actionable findings.

Review threads addressed (all on #104171): channel normalization, hidden-nav affordance, launch-path prerelease sharing, prerelease repair policy, native-decline fallback, pending-restart prompt duplication.

target.title: fix: resolve lint and type checking errors
target.body:
### What Problem This Solves
This PR fixes several issues that were causing CI and local linting/type-checking (`npm run lint:all`) to fail:
1. **Invalid oxlint rule**: Removed the non-existent `unicorn/no-array-fill-with-reference-type` rule from `.oxlintrc.json` which was causing `oxlint` to crash.
2. **Missing type declarations**: Added ambient types for `markdown-it-cjk-friendly` in `packages/markdown-core`, resolving the `plugin-sdk` boundary type check error (TS2307).
3. **Outdated Telegram types**: Removed `supports_join_request_queries` from `UserFromGetMe` references in the `telegram` extension, as this property has been removed from `grammy/types` (fixing TS2561).

### Evidence
Verified that local linting and the telegram extension tests pass successfully after these type definition and config changes. 

Terminal output for tests:
```text

- [x] Will resolve or reply to bot review conversations if any arise.

*(Note: AI prompts and session context were used to identify the broken typescript configurations and oxlint rules and apply the precise fixes.)*
